findings.title: Observer state is pruned to the current project, defeating the poll interval and fault recurrence
findings.description:
`RunnerTenant.__init__` builds one `RunObserver` (`src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py`, `observer=self._observer`) and hands that same instance to every `ProjectTick` (`src/amoeba/runner/tenant.py#RunnerTenant._tick_project`). Each project's tick calls `observe()` with **only its own** unresolved entries (`src/amoeba/runner/tick.py`, `self._observer.observe(self._run_entries(), ...)`, where `_run_entries` filters on `self._project_id`). `observe()` then discards every entry id not in that project's set:

```python
live = {entry.id for entry in entries}
self._last_poll = {k: v for k, v in self._last_poll.items() if k in live}
self._overdue &= live
self._faulted = {k: v for k, v in self._faulted.items() if k in live}
```

With projects `a` and `b` that each have an in-flight run, the tick order is `[a, b]`. `a`'s pass records `_last_poll[a1]` and polls; `b`'s pass immediately deletes it. On the next tick `_poll_due(a1)` sees `last is None` and returns `True`, so `a1` is polled again on a tick that is roughly one `idle_interval_seconds` later — not after `run_poll_interval_seconds`. The same mechanism silently drops `_overdue` and `_faulted` between two ticks of the same project, so:

- The `launch_overdue` fault stops recurring, and `ProjectTick._close_recovered` therefore closes the escalation on the very next COMPLETE tick, only for it to be re-raised and re-opened on the tick after — escalation churn on the feed, which is exactly what the comment above `_faulted` says the replay exists to prevent ("replayed on ticks between polls so a fault that stands does not look recovered (and its escalation close)").
- A standing `run_observation_failed` fault likewise disappears for a tick and its escalation closes and re-opens.

This contradicts the slice's own success criterion ("A confirmed in-flight run is polled no more than once per tick and no more often than `run_poll_interval_seconds`") and `docs/process-contract.md`'s "at most once per tick per run and no more often than `--run-poll-interval`, least recently polled first". It is also the exact cost the design measured and built the interval to avoid (≈1 s wall and ≈0.7 s CPU per `sq runs wait` call, per the slice design's D10 rationale) — here it is paid once per project per tick.

Single-project supervisors are unaffected, which is why the whole `tests/runner/` suite is green: `test_tenant.py` registers multiple projects but never gives two of them concurrent in-flight entries, and `observe_support.Rig` / `tick_support.Rig` are single-project. Keying the three dictionaries by project as well as entry (or holding one observer per project) fixes it; a regression test with two projects each holding an in-flight run is what is missing.

findings.title: Squadron's "usage error" exit code 2 is defined in two places
findings.description: `src/amoeba/process/sq_outcome.py:51` establishes the fact in prose and delegates it: "Squadron's exit code for each outcome. Usage errors exit 2 and are not here." `src/amoeba/runner/observe.py` then re-states the same Squadron contract as a literal, `USAGE_ERROR_EXIT_CODE = 2`, and compares against it at `src/amoeba/runner/observe.py:245`. This is the case AGENTS.md names directly — "Never scatter comparison values across code… define it once (enum, constant, or config)" — and `USAGE_ERROR_EXIT_CODE` reaches the process-level decision in `ProjectTick._record_finished` that raises `UpstreamShapeError` and exits with `UPSTREAM_SHAPE`. `amoeba.process` is already an allowed import root for the Runner under boundary rule 11, so the constant can live once in `sq_outcome.py` (beside `OUTCOME_EXIT_CODES`) and be exported; changing Squadron's usage exit code should require editing one file, not three.

findings.title: The "exactly one broad except" test asserts on file text, not on syntax
findings.description: `test_the_runner_package_has_exactly_one_broad_except` counts `path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").count("except Exception")` over every `*.py` in `src/amoeba/runner`. That is a substring count, so it passes just as happily for `except BaseException as error:` (which would catch `KeyboardInterrupt` and `SystemExit` at this boundary), for `except Exception:` in a comment or docstring, and it would silently become `2` if a comment quoted the phrase. The invariant the slice actually needs — one broad handler, at the documented process boundary in `tenant.py` — is stated in the module docstring and enforced only by this count. Parsing the AST and asserting on `ast.ExceptHandler` nodes whose `type` is `Exception` (and on which file they appear in) tests the property rather than a rendering of it.

findings.title: `build_argv` is called twice per launch: once to validate, once to execute
findings.description: `_launch` calls `build_argv(action.pipeline, run_id, action.params)` purely for its side effect (the `ValueError` before journaling, as the inline comment says) and discards the result; `launch()` then rebuilds the same argv from the journal entry's parameters. The two calls agree today because `journal_issue` round-trips `str` values through JSON and `_params_parameter` re-checks them, but "what was validated" and "what is executed" are two different computations. Passing the validated argv into `launch()` (or extracting the parameter check into one function both call) would keep D2's "call this before journaling" guarantee without relying on the two paths staying in lock-step.

findings.title: Slice document still records `UPSTREAM_SHAPE` as exit code 8
findings.description: Under "API Contracts" the slice design says "New exit code `UPSTREAM_SHAPE` (8): a launch exited 2…". The implementation uses 15, with a comment explaining why (`src/amoeba/cli/main.py`: "8 is already `NOT_RUNNING_STATUS`, so this is the next free value"), and `tests/test_cli_lifecycle.py` pins 15. `docs/process-contract.md` and the CHANGELOG agree with the code, so only the slice design's API-contract line is stale. It is the artifact a reader consults before wiring a consumer to this exit code.

findings.title: Block-then-resolve is idempotent and the crash proof exercises it
findings.description: I checked the ordering claim rather than taking it from the hunk. Every path through `record` writes the block before `journal_resolve`, `_block_once` returns early when `store.blocked_state_for(entry.node_id)` is not `None`, and `Store.block` itself refuses a second block (`_refuse_if_blocked`). The `BETWEEN_BLOCK_AND_RESOLVE` kill point in `tests/runner/crash_entry.py` (which patches `Store.journal_resolve` to `SIGKILL` itself) plus `test_kill_between_block_and_resolve_finishes_the_sequence` asserting `len(harness.open_blocks(...)) == 1` is the right test for that invariant, and it is written as a real subprocess crash rather than a mocked one.

findings.title: Exception handling follows the specific-type discipline the project requires
findings.description: Reading the modules rather than the diff: every `except` in `src/amoeba/runner/` names a specific type with an inline justification (`OSError` in `launch()` and `_tail_or_error`, `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and `OSError` in `probe_link`, `OSError` in `_check_line`), and the single broad handler is the per-project boundary in `tenant.py`, where it logs with `logger.exception`, escalates, and deliberately lets a failing escalation write propagate. `STORE_FAILURES` and `UpstreamShapeError` re-raise before it, so a broken store still stops the process instead of running blind. That matches both the project rule and the slice's D8.

structured_findings.summary: Observer state is pruned to the current project, defeating the poll interval and fault recurrence
Squadron's "usage error" exit code 2 is defined in two places
The "exactly one broad except" test asserts on file text, not on syntax
`build_argv` is called twice per launch: once to validate, once to execute
Slice document still records `UPSTREAM_SHAPE` as exit code 8
Block-then-resolve is idempotent and the crash proof exercises it
Exception handling follows the specific-type discipline the project requires
